newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar drifts off highs, trade routine.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar drifts off highs, trade routine.

text.p: London white sugar futures remained confined to tight ranges in listless Friday trading, reflecting the lack of movement on the New York raws market.
Values were firmer earlier in the session but then eased slightly after the raws open, with a number of crossed trades boosting overall volume.
At 1524 GMT December was up just 40 cents at $327.50 after moving in a tight $1.10 range. March was off 90 cents and turnover totalled 1,765 lots.
Traders noted some shortcovering of positions ahead of the weekend but said activity was otherwise routine.
Technically, December is still clinging to values around $328, its nearby support level for most of this week.

Technical analysts said while December's RSI (Relative Strength Index) continued to hover just above oversold levels, further selling pressure could be expected. In physical news, Syria was reported to have bought 13,000 tonnes of raw sugar at $311.50 per tonne c & f for November shipment, to include bagging costs. Details of the supplier have yet to emerge.
Earlier on Friday, market sources said Syria bought a cargo of white sugar at $368.95 per tonne, with the supplier believed to be a European trade house.
In Paris white sugar futures lost ground in a total volume of 1,345 lots. December and March were both down $1.00, at $327.00 and $324.00 respectively.
